title: A space to shape.
description: The Centra Sculpt field guide. Start with a little clay. Leave with something you made.
body:
MAKE SOMETHING YOURS

Centra Sculpt is a browser-based sculpting and precision modelling workspace. Shape clay on desktop, work around it in Quest 3, or combine editable solids into a measured part. You can start small: a sphere, a few strokes and your first exported mesh.

Your first clay sculpt ↗From a starter sphere to a saved, editable project.Step into VR ↗Learn the Tool hand, Support hand and Tool Wheel.Make with an agent ↗Local MCP access, with you approving changes.

Pick a way to work

For organic forms, sculpt a voxel layer: a small 3D grid that describes where solid material exists. For a measured bracket or enclosure, start with parametric primitives: solids whose dimensions remain editable. Boolean operations join these solids or use one to cut another. Bake a result into clay when you want to brush or paint it.

A manual for the current app

This guide covers Phase 7.6.1, checked against local source on 10 November 2026. Built-in Stamp shapes are available. Personal Shapes saves reusable sculpt geometry; learn to save and insert it. Using personal shapes as stamps remains deferred to 8.0.1. Quest hardware and physical print acceptance are separate from automated software checks.

Open this guide from Centra Sculpt → Help in the app menu. Use the full text navigation to browse every guide, or search with Cmd/Ctrl + K. All reading and search runs on this static site; no account or API key is required.

Make a useful part

Try the illustrated practical holder and printable enclosure tutorials. Use Choose how to build to pick a tool, or look up unfamiliar words in the glossary.

title: Your first clay sculpt
description: Create, shape, smooth and save a small pebble. Allow about 10 minutes.
body:
Before you begin

You need the desktop editor, a mouse or trackpad and somewhere to keep a downloaded .form file. Save any existing project first. This exercise makes a free-form pebble; it does not depend on physical dimensions.

1. Create your starting clay

  1. Open the Centra Sculpt logo menu → New Project.
  2. Enter a project name. Choose 64³ and Starter sphere under Start with, then Create Project.
  3. Use right drag to orbit and scroll to zoom until the sphere fills the middle of the viewport.

2. Shape a small ridge

  1. Choose Add under Sculpt Brush. Leave a broad radius and gentle strength.
  2. Drag one short stroke or a few dabs across the visible surface. Release before starting the next stroke.
  3. Orbit and inspect. Choose Subtract for a shallow hollow if you like.
  4. If the result is too strong, use Cmd/Ctrl + Z and try a shorter stroke.

3. Soften the surface

  1. Choose Smooth.
  2. Drag a short stroke over the ridge, then release and inspect from another angle.
  3. Stop while the overall shape still feels intentional. Repeated smoothing can erase a small feature.

4. Save a project you can return to

  1. Click the header Save icon to save in the browser project library.
  2. Open the logo menu → Library and check the saved entry.
  3. Use the project details → Download .form, or hold the header Save icon to download a native copy.
  4. Keep that file in a backed-up folder. STL and GLB are mesh exports, not editable project backups.

Expected outcome: a gently shaped clay object, a browser library entry and an editable .form backup.

Desktop or Quest?

Desktop uses left drag for brushing, right drag for orbit and scroll for zoom. On Quest, select Clay then Smooth from the Tool Wheel; hold Tool trigger to stroke and release to finish. Support grip moves the workspace. For saving and file hand-off, see Projects. Quest screenshots are pending; the images above show desktop.

If something feels wrong

  • Dragging moves the layer: press B to return to Sculpt.
  • No brush change: select an unlocked clay layer and check the mask. A primitive needs Bake to Sculpt Layer first.
  • A stroke is interrupted: release, wait for the editor to be ready and try a shorter, slower stroke.
  • Too much material disappears: undo, lower strength and make one pass at a time.

Try next

Keep the .form, then try painting or exporting. For dimensioned parts, continue with the three-slot holder.

title: Find your way on desktop
description: The workspace, camera and keyboard shortcuts.
body:
The workspace

The left panel holds sculpt brushes, settings, project actions and Export…. The centre is the viewport. The right panel holds Layers, Surface View and layer transforms. Scroll the left panel for Primitives, Measure & precision, Enclosure and Assembly. Some sections are collapsible; open their heading to reveal controls.

The logo opens New Project, Open Project, Library, Help and About. Help opens this guide in a new tab, keeping the editor open. The Save icon reports save state. The viewport offers rendering style, camera views and Frame selected. Rendering styles Normal, Matte and Glossy help inspect a surface; they are display choices, separate from painted colour.

Camera and editing shortcuts

InputAction
Right drag / scrollOrbit / zoom
Shift + right drag or middle dragPan
.Frame selected layer or group
BSculpt; hide shape ghost
W / E / RLayer Move / Rotate / Scale
Hold E / D / C during MoveConstrain X / Y / Z
Hold R / F / V during RotateConstrain X / Y / Z
G / TMove / rotate stamp ghost; press again to finish
ICycle rendering style
Delete / BackspaceDelete selected layer, undoable
Cmd/Ctrl + ZUndo
Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + ZRedo
Cmd/Ctrl + SSave project

Shortcuts are context-sensitive. For example E selects Rotate when idle, but constrains X during a Move. Finish typing in a numeric field before using modelling shortcuts. Escape cancels supported active tools; in export it cancels work or closes the idle dialog.

Run locally

npm install
npm run dev

Run these in the repository, then open the URL printed by Vite. Normal development mode does not start the MCP bridge. Desktop and VR edit the same project, but file import is performed through the desktop file picker.

title: Set up Quest 3 & controllers
description: Learn roles before gestures.
body:
Open the editor in WebXR

Use Quest Browser with a WebXR-capable secure origin. For local headset development run npm run dev:https, follow the printed HTTPS address and the repository certificate setup, and ensure your headset trusts the certificate. A desktop localhost exception does not make a LAN HTTP address a secure WebXR origin. Both devices need network access to the host.

Open your project and import references on desktop first. In VR / WEBXR DIAGNOSTICS choose Dominant Tool Hand, then Enter VR. Tool defaults to right, Support to left. Physical left stays cyan and right amber when roles swap. Diagnostics can help identify tracking and role problems.

Local headset setup: USB localhost

With Quest Developer Mode enabled, Android platform-tools installed and USB debugging approved in the headset, the repository’s USB route avoids development-certificate trust problems. Start npm run dev on the host, then:

adb devices -l
adb reverse tcp:5173 tcp:5173
adb reverse --list

Open http://localhost:5173/ in Quest Browser. This is forwarded headset loopback, which qualifies for the localhost secure-context exception. Remove forwarding afterwards with adb reverse --remove tcp:5173. Use the actual port if you changed it.

Wireless HTTPS setup

The launcher uses port 5174 and expects .certs/centra-cert.pem and .certs/centra-key.pem. Generate a matching certificate for your host with your chosen local certificate tool, then establish issuer trust on Quest. Host trust alone and clicking past a warning are insufficient. If the headset cannot trust the issuer, use USB localhost. Do not share private certificate keys.

The two roles

ControlWhat it does
Tool triggerHold to sculpt; tap to stamp or select a menu item. Move holds deform and release commits.
Tool stick up/downChange brush/Move radius or stamp size while idle.
Support stick left/rightUndo / Redo, idle only. Centre to rearm.
Support stick up/downHold up for Tool Wheel; hold down for Layers. Point with Tool ray and use Tool trigger. Release the Support stick to close.
Support triggerHold alternate brush; Options configures it. Release restores after the stroke.
Support gripGrab workspace for navigation.
Tool gripTransform Layer: manipulate the layer. Stamp: adjust attachment offset.
Both gripsMove, rotate and scale the workspace; release either grip to end the two-hand gesture.

Workspace navigation changes how the scene sits around you; it does not change the model’s physical dimensions. Layer transforms do change the model. Face buttons and system controls are not substitutes for the documented Support-stick menu bindings.

If input stops responding

Release triggers, grips and sticks, then try again. Tracking loss, system overlays or a role swap cancel holds and require fresh presses. A lost controller pose hides stale visuals. If Enter VR is unavailable, check HTTPS trust, browser permissions and WebXR support first. This guide describes implemented controls; no fresh Quest hardware acceptance was performed for this documentation update.

Screenshot status

Quest Tool Wheel, Options, Layers, precision, enclosure and assembly captures are pending authentic headset capture. The interactive wheel guide is explicitly a source-accurate schematic, not a headset screenshot. Desktop captures elsewhere do not establish hardware acceptance.

title: The complete Tool Wheel
description: Where every wheel item and nested path leads.
body:
Explore the wheel

Source-accurate schematic — not a Quest screenshot. Nine sectors in source order from VR_WHEEL_TOOLS. Button placement below is adapted for readable documentation and does not reproduce headset geometry. Authentic Quest captures are pending.

Select a tool with mouse or touch. Keyboard: Tab to a tool, Enter or Space to select; arrow keys, Home and End move between tool buttons.

Clay

Add or subtract material.

Options → operation, placement, Steady, Straight Line, spacing and quality.

Read the Clay guide →

Smooth

Soften bumps and blend strokes.

Options → brush settings.

Read the Smooth guide →

Flatten

Relax the surface towards a local tangent plane.

Options → brush settings.

Read the Flatten guide →

Inflate

Expand the local surface.

Options → brush settings.

Read the Inflate guide →

Stamp

Apply a built-in shape to clay.

Options → Shape, operation, single/continuous, dimensions and wrist offsets.

Read the Stamp guide →

Move Tool

Deform a surface region; release commits.

Options → Move variants → Non-Elastic Move, Elastic Move, Rotate / Twist, Pinch, Crease or Scrape → Variant settings.

Read the Move Tool guide →

Tube

Draw a path-based tube and edit spline points.

Options → target, draw and spline selection/edit controls.

Read the Tube guide →

Transform Layer

Move or rotate the whole selected layer.

Options → pose, uniform scale, Surface view, reset confirmation and snapping.

Read the Transform Layer guide →

Cut

Split clay into separate pieces with a plane.

Plane Cut → normal, offset, scope, tilt → Preview Plane → Apply Cut · create new layer.

Read the Cut guide →

Options belongs to the current tool. Paint, Mask, Project, World Settings and Snap 15° are additional controls around the wheel, not extra sectors. See the paths below.

Open, point, choose

Hold Support stick up. Point the Tool ray at an item and tap Tool trigger. The centre Options button shows settings for the current tool; paged settings use previous/next arrows. Menu size switches Standard / Large. Support stick down opens Layers independently.

Wheel sector, in source orderUse / nested path
ClayAdd / subtract; Options includes operation, placement, Steady, Straight Line, spacing and quality.
SmoothSoften surfaces; brush settings in Options.
FlattenRelax towards a local tangent plane.
InflateExpand the local surface.
StampOptions → Shape, operation, single/continuous mode, dimensions, wrist offsets and attachment reset.
Move ToolOptions → Move variants → Non-Elastic Move, Elastic Move, Rotate / Twist, Pinch, Crease, Scrape → Variant settings.
TubeDraw a tube; Options includes target, draw and spline selection/edit controls.
Transform LayerOptions → move/rotation values, uniform scale, Surface view, selected layer, Reset Layer Transform confirmation and snapping settings.
CutPlane Cut → X/Y/Z normal, offset, affected scope, tilt → Preview Plane → review → Apply Cut · create new layer. Adjust or cancel before applying.

Buttons around the wheel

Mask and Paint are separate bottom buttons, alongside Project. World Settings and Snap 15° sit above the sectors. Snap 15° applies to Straight Line direction and Move rotation; it is muted when irrelevant. It is separate from surface snapping and physical position snapping.

World Settings and Project

World Settings opens Project Library, Environment, Studio Background, Guides and Constraints, Measure & Precision, Preferences, Lighting, References and Turntable. Further pages expose guide/mirror settings, reference selection and precise pose/more settings/deletion, lighting/ambient/inspection/colour/position, environment/background, and turntable pivot controls. Project opens the project-library workflow. File import uses the desktop picker; exit XR to import then re-enter.

Layers menu

Select a layer, toggle Visible/Hidden or Locked/Unlocked, add a new layer and use Merge with…. The palette also supports the hierarchy/group workflow. Merge has a layer choice, output resolution and explicit confirmation; originals are kept hidden. A disabled control can mean a busy tool, a locked selection, incompatible source or the 16-layer capacity.

Nested layer and precision paths

Layers → More opens Layer Options: duplicate, rename, attach/detach, resolution, move up/down and Boolean order…. Group Options adds Ungroup and Delete group confirmation, with choices to keep or delete children. Boolean order opens the ordered sequence and Live Boolean Shapes…; that page selects sources/modifiers, changes operation, enables/disables, removes, edits source or bakes the visible result. Resolution changes have a confirmation.

World Settings → Measure & Precision opens distance, three-point angle, units, selected dimensions, position snap, angle snap, calibration, annotations and Precision transforms…. Numeric entry has Apply/Cancel. Annotations offers next/remove/reposition. Primitives… opens the editable primitive workflow. Project Library has project details and confirmation pages; available file operations can hand off to the desktop browser.

title: Sculpt with brushes
description: Build the big form first; refine the surface second.
body:
Choose the right brush

BrushGood for
Clay Add / SubtractBuilding mass or carving a hollow.
SmoothSoftening bumps and blending strokes.
FlattenLevelling towards a local tangent plane. It is not a dimensioned machining operation.
InflateExpanding the surface along local normals.
ScrapeRemoving raised material above the applicator plane.
PinchDrawing nearby clay tangentially into a ridge.
CreasePinching with inward displacement for a narrow groove.

On desktop these are in Sculpt Brush. In VR, Pinch, Crease and Scrape live under Move Tool → Options → Move variants. Adjust radius, strength and the selected tool’s options. Paint and Mask use their own modes; see colour and protection.

Resolution and stroke quality

A 64³ layer has 64 samples along each axis, not 64 triangles. Higher resolution can capture smaller changes, at a memory cost. Resample offers 64³, 128³ and 192³ and clears sculpt undo for that layer. Save a native copy before changing resolution. Increasing it cannot restore detail already lost.

Steady helps stabilise a stroke. Straight Line constrains the path; its axis is layer-local. Direction snapping can use 15° steps. Geometry quality and VR stroke options affect tool behaviour; they do not lift export limits. Try a low-strength stroke, inspect from another angle, then repeat instead of removing too much in one pass.

Symmetry and turntable

Mirror symmetry uses a plane in the layer’s local coordinates. Adjust its normal and offset when the result does not mirror where expected. Guides and Constraints control guides; Turntable offers speed, angle reset and pivot settings. Workspace movement and turntable presentation should not be mistaken for exact model sizing.

title: Move, Tube & Stamp
description: Three different ways to change or build a form.
body:
Move Tool: deform a region

Move Tool changes the surface inside an influence radius; Transform Layer moves the whole layer. Choose Non-Elastic Move for a direct deformation, Elastic Move for a softer response, or Rotate / Twist for a rotational gesture. Options expose radius, edge softness, translation strength, elastic firmness, precision, axis constraints, wrist sensitivity, angle limit and rotation snapping where applicable.

In VR hold Tool trigger to deform and release to commit. Finish or cancel Move before saving/exporting or starting another operation. A cancelled or interrupted interaction should not be treated as a completed edit. Use Undo if the committed result is wrong.

Tube: draw, then edit

Tube creates a procedural tube along a path. Choose the target and draw settings, then draw with the tool. Switch to spline editing to grab control points; adjust a point radius or the whole tube radius through Options. Insert/delete point controls are available for the selected spline. A tube remains editable as a path until baked. Use it for a handle or cable-like form, then inspect tight bends and joins.

Stamp: built-in shapes on clay

Stamp applies a shape into the active sculpt layer using Add or Subtract. Its built-in shapes are Sphere, Cube / Box, Triangular Prism and Square Pyramid. A sphere uses equal diameters; the stamp pyramid has a square base. These are distinct from the editable primitive layers.

Place and inspect the ghost before applying. Desktop G moves it and T rotates it; press the same key again to finish. In VR a trigger tap applies a single stamp. Options also provides continuous mode and spacing as a fraction of the smallest shape dimension. Tool grip adjusts attachment offset; reset the offset when placement feels unexpected. B returns to brushing on desktop.

Personal Shapes saves reusable sculpt geometry for independent editable insertion. See save and reuse shapes. Personal shapes as sculpting stamps remain deferred to 8.0.1; built-in Stamp does not import arbitrary custom assets.

title: Create editable primitives
description: Start with dimensions you can change later.
body:
Create, position, revise

Open Primitives → Create new. Choose a shape, enter dimensions in the displayed physical units and use the shape-specific button, such as Create Box. New primitives start at the model origin. Move them with transforms or Position, rotation & scale. Select a primitive in Layers, then Edit selected to revise dimensions. Restore initial dimensions returns to its creation dimensions and supports Undo.

PrimitiveDimensions and useful details
BoxIndependent width, height, depth; rounded-box source support is also used by enclosures.
SphereDiameter, with independent ellipsoid axes supported.
CylinderHeight and end diameters; unequal ends form a capped frustum.
ConeA cylinder-family preset with zero top diameter. Base diameter, tip diameter and height remain editable.
CapsuleDiameter and overall height, including both rounded ends. Height must be at least the diameter.
TorusRing radius to the tube centre and tube diameter. The ring lies in XZ. Tyre shape 0–100 changes the cross-section from round towards a rounded tyre profile.
PyramidWidth, height and depth; apex points along +Y. Unlike the built-in stamp, primitive width/depth can differ.

For a torus with ring radius 20 mm and tube diameter 8 mm, outside diameter is 48 mm and the hole diameter is 32 mm. The ring radius must exceed half the tube diameter. Very thin/extreme shapes can be refused by aspect, physical or sampling limits; split the design into sensible parts.

When to Bake

Parametric dimensions describe an editable source. Bake to Sculpt Layer creates brushable geometry while keeping the source. Use this before sculpting, cutting or painting a primitive. Bake samples the shape at finite resolution: cone tips, thin walls and small holes may lose detail. Save first, choose enough detail, inspect, and retain the original source until satisfied.

If a dimension is refused

Read the validation message before creating, then check the created source’s physical bounds readout. Intermediate aspect ratios matter: when changing a large cube into a narrow cutter, reduce height and depth before entering the narrow width. A rejected field does not mean the source has that dimension.

title: Measure, calibrate & transform
description: Physical size starts in the project, before export.
body:
Model units and physical units

Measure & precision offers mm, cm and inches. New and legacy projects begin at 100 mm per model unit. Calibration changes physical interpretation, not the stored surface. For example, a 2-model-unit width at 100 mm/unit represents 200 mm. Moving the VR workspace closer does not change this size.

Place measurements

Choose Measure distance and place two model points. Measure angle uses three points, with point 2 as the vertex. Stop measuring when finished. Review annotations lets you remove a measurement or reposition its points. Annotations stay at the placed model points; recheck them after changing the model.

Enter an exact transform

Use Position · model axes and Rotation · XYZ degrees in Measure & precision for physical input. Enter or Tab applies; Escape cancels. Uniform scale changes all axes together. Target dimensions preserve proportions: entering a width changes height and depth too. To change only a primitive’s shape, edit its dimensions in Primitives.

The Active Layer Numeric Transform panel uses absolute project/world coordinates. Read its unit label: these model values differ from the physical fields. Gizmo space can be World or Local. Desktop Move uses W, Rotate E and Scale R; select the layer first. Primitive scale handles can edit their supported local dimensions, while other layers scale uniformly.

Snapping choices

Position snap and angle step help repeat exact transforms; zero angle step turns angle snapping off. The Tool Wheel’s Snap 15° controls Line/Move rotation direction. Surface snapping aligns one object to a target surface. These are separate settings, so check the relevant one when a tool seems constrained.

title: Layers, groups & safe Bake
description: Keep editable ingredients until you are happy with the result.
body:
Organise the scene

A layer is an independently editable source: clay, a primitive or a tube. Groups organise children and let you transform a collection. Rename entries and press Enter to apply, select them in Layers, and use visibility, locking and hierarchy controls to keep the scene manageable. Collapse groups to reduce clutter. The current capacity is 16 sculpt/source layers. Groups have a separate limit of 32, with nesting up to eight levels.

Visibility controls display/export participation; locks prevent edits. A hidden object can still be a referenced Boolean operand. Hiding a cutter is therefore not the same as disabling its modifier. Check the graph when an invisible source still affects the result.

Source versus evaluated result

Surface View → Layers shows separate source layers. Boolean shows the composed, evaluated surface after ordered operations. Think of sources as ingredients and the evaluated surface as the dish. Editing a source updates the result; merely switching view does not bake or replace the sources.

Editable sources→Booleans + arrays→Preview / Export / Bake

Interactive Boolean detail can reduce to fit frame-rate or work budgets, then refine after release. A Reduced detail status describes a display approximation. Export has its own resolution and admission checks, and may still refuse the same scene.

Bake without losing your way back

  1. Save a native project copy and inspect the Boolean preview.
  2. Open Bake / Merge…. Choose a result name and output resolution: 64³, 128³ or 192³.
  3. Leave Hide source layers after baking enabled unless you deliberately need both visible.
  4. Bake new layer, wait, then inspect small holes and edges. Cancel if needed while working.

Bake creates a sampled sculpt layer, keeping the sources. Lower resolution can remove detail. Merge two layers instead forms a union and keeps originals hidden. Avoid showing originals alongside the baked result when checking size or exporting; duplicate geometry can confuse your result. Undo reverses the committed operation.

title: Booleans & arrays
description: Join solids, cut openings and repeat a design.
body:
Three Boolean operations

Union keeps material from either shape. Difference removes the operand from the target. Intersect keeps only their shared volume. Ordered layer operations and explicit live modifiers both exist; their order matters. A difference applied before another union can give a different result.

Select the target layer and use its Boolean controls to choose the operand and operation. Keep the cutters editable. Switch Surface View to Boolean to inspect the composed result. Make a through-cutter extend beyond both faces, rather than relying on coincident surfaces. References are visual aids, not Boolean solids.

Example: a slotted holder

Create a box for the body, another for the base and three narrow boxes for slots. Union the overlapping base into the body, then subtract each slot cutter. Check the evaluated view before export. The agent holder walkthrough gives exact dimensions and the same editable graph as a reproducible example.

Array / Repeat

Under Primitives, open Array / Repeat. Linear repetition spaces copies along a direction; radial repetition distributes them around an axis/pivot. Inspect count, spacing or angle and transform settings before applying. An array is an evaluated repetition of a source, not a free increase in layer or work capacity. Every instance contributes to evaluation work.

Change the original to update its repeated result. Use the array controls to update or remove repetition. Surface bounds and radial spacing can differ from the source dimensions. Inspect the final result for overlapping copies, thin gaps and unintended joins. Bake only when you need brushable clay, keeping an editable native copy first.

Plane Cut is different

Plane Cut splits a sculpt layer into two closed pieces; it is not a Boolean operand modifier. Choose axis, offset and tilt, preview the plane and confirm. Scope can be Active layer or All visible, unlocked SDF layers. The second piece becomes a new layer; paint/masks are retained, and new cut faces inherit nearby paint samples.

title: Place objects on a surface
description: Use a target surface to guide placement and alignment.
body:
Choose the target and placement

Surface snap settings are available in Transform options. Choose snap targets and target radius, enable Surface snap and choose placement behaviour. Set a surface offset in mm when the object should sit above or below the hit. Local alignment axis, Flip surface normal and Rotate about normal control orientation.

Targets can include eligible visible model geometry and imported STL reference surfaces. Centre/face target snapping uses visible target bounds; surface hits use the mesh surface. The moving object is excluded from its own targets. Inspect the chosen target when objects are close together.

Example: place a foot on a curved body

  1. Select the foot and enter Transform mode.
  2. Enable surface snapping and choose the body as a suitable target.
  3. Set the foot’s local alignment axis and place it against the surface.
  4. Flip the normal if it points inward; rotate about the normal for the desired direction.
  5. Inspect side and isometric views, then check overlap or clearance numerically.

Snapping provides placement, not a guaranteed mechanical joint. It follows the available mesh and its resolution. A reference STL can guide placement without becoming exported material.

title: Build a practical holder
description: Build a measured body and base, subtract three slots and prepare an STL. Allow 25–40 minutes.
body:
Before you begin

Use desktop for numeric entry. Start a new project with Empty scene at 64³, and keep the empty layer hidden. You need five free source-layer slots, familiarity with Primitives, and a slicer to inspect the exported mesh. These are teaching dimensions, not measurements of a previously printed user project.

1. Create the body and base

  1. In Primitives → Create new, choose Box. Enter width 90, height 20 and depth 40 mm, then Create Box.
  2. Rename it Body in Layers and press Enter. Open Primitives → Position, rotation & scale. Set Position X 0, Y 13, Z 0 in mm; press Enter to apply each field. Keep rotation zero and scale 1.
  3. Create a second Box, width 110, height 16, depth 50 mm. Rename it Base plate and press Enter. Set its physical position to X 0, Y 4, Z 0.
  4. Select Body in Layers. Expand its Live Boolean Shapes, choose Base plate as Boolean source operand, then Add / Union.

The 9 mm overlap joins the base and body. Do not use the separate Active Layer Numeric Transform fields for these mm values: those fields use model units.

2. Make three cutters

  1. Choose Create new → Box. Enter height 22 mm, depth 14 mm, then width 8 mm, in that order. Choose Create Box, then check the physical bounds readout is 8 × 22 × 14 mm. If a dimension was refused, undo and correct it before continuing. Rename it Left slot and press Enter.
  2. Set its physical position to X −24, Y 13, Z 0 mm.
  3. Create two more boxes with the same dimensions, again entering height and depth before the narrow width. Rename them Centre slot and Right slot, pressing Enter for each; position them at X 0 and +24 respectively, keeping Y 13 and Z 0.
  4. Select Body. In Live Boolean Shapes choose Left slot, then Subtract / Difference. Repeat for Centre slot and Right slot.

Each cutter extends 1 mm above and below the 20 mm body. It cuts into the overlapping base without passing through the entire base, leaving a floor.

3. Inspect and save

  1. Switch Surface View to Boolean. Hide independent operand roots if they obscure inspection; referenced operands still affect Body.
  2. Orbit and check three openings and a connected base. Body should have one union followed by three differences.
  3. When preparing the export in the next step, check evaluated dimensions: XYZ should be approximately 110 × 27 × 50 mm. Source bounds alone do not verify the cut result.
  4. Save in the browser and download a .form copy before exporting.

4. Prepare the STL

  1. Open Export…. Choose STL, Standard initially and Actual size (1:1).
  2. Choose Unified Boolean so the cutters are evaluated. Current layer is refused while live modifiers or arrays are present.
  3. Wait for preparation. Review XYZ size, warnings and Print report, then download.
  4. Open the STL in a slicer, confirm millimetres and inspect all three slots and the floor in section view.

Expected outcome: an editable five-source design with three slots and a reviewed STL. A slicer check and a small clearance test are still needed before relying on a print.

When the result differs

  • A narrow dimension is refused: set height and depth first, then width, and check the bounds readout. Intermediate extreme aspect ratios can be refused even when your final design is valid.
  • No slots: check Body is the target and all three difference modifiers are enabled.
  • Unexpected size: check mm fields, calibration, scale 1 and Actual size (1:1).
  • Reduced-detail preview: it is a display approximation. Export has separate strict limits.
  • Work or memory refusal: simplify or export smaller parts; do not keep raising detail.

Quest and next steps

Quest uses Layers → More → Boolean order… → Live Boolean Shapes…, and World Settings → Measure & Precision → Primitives…. Numeric entry is easier on desktop. Quest captures are pending. Next try a separate box and lid, or use the reproducible agent batch below.

Optional: reproduce with an agent

Plan the geometry

The body is 90 × 20 × 40 mm at [0,13,0]. The base is 110 × 16 × 50 mm at [0,4,0], overlapping it by 9 mm. Three 8 × 22 × 14 mm cutters sit at X −24, 0 and +24, Y 13, Z 0. Union the base into the body, then subtract each cutter. Expected evaluated XYZ bounds are 110 × 27 × 50 mm. This is an editable fixture, not a certified fitted product.

Body ∪ base→− left − centre − right→Evaluated holder

Submit the exact batch

First call scene_summary and replace LATEST_REVISION. The following is the argument object for propose_changes, not a shell command. It uses 14 commands and five layer slots. Dimensions/positions use explicit mm; object.transform rotations use XYZ radians, here all zero.

{
  "expectedRevision": "LATEST_REVISION",
  "title": "90 mm three-slot holder with 110 mm base",
  "description": "Create a 90 \u00d7 20 \u00d7 40 mm body, three 8 \u00d7 22 \u00d7 14 mm slot cutters at X \u221224/0/+24 mm, and a 110 \u00d7 16 \u00d7 50 mm base at Y 4 mm. Union the base, subtract the cutters, then inspect bounds and front/isometric captures.",
  "steps": [
    {
      "as": "body",
      "command": {
        "type": "primitive.create",
        "unit": "mm",
        "source": {
          "kind": "box",
          "width": 90,
          "height": 20,
          "depth": 40
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "command": {
        "type": "object.transform",
        "id": "$body",
        "unit": "mm",
        "transform": {
          "position": [
            0,
            13,
            0
          ],
          "rotation": [
            0,
            0,
            0
          ],
          "scale": [
            1,
            1,
            1
          ]
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "as": "base",

Aliases refer to earlier results in this batch; provisional preview IDs are not stable applied IDs. The browser shows the staged plan without changing scene/history. Ask the person to review and approve it there, then call get_proposal and apply_approved_proposal with the returned proposal ID (these proposal tools take proposalId, not an extra expectedRevision). An agent cannot approve its own proposal.

A staged proposal expires after two minutes. If it expires or the scene changes, inspect current state and rebuild the plan rather than applying stale work.

get_proposal {"proposalId":"RETURNED_PROPOSAL_ID"}
# Only after the person approves in the browser:
apply_approved_proposal {"proposalId":"RETURNED_PROPOSAL_ID"}
# Read calls after application:
get_booleans {"id":"APPLIED_BODY_ID"}
get_bounds {"id":"APPLIED_BODY_ID"}

capture_scene_preview {"objectId":"APPLIED_BODY_ID","viewpoint":"isometric"}
# If the latest action is still this batch and undo is intended:
undo {"expectedRevision":"LATEST_REVISION"}

Verify the result

Read the applied object IDs and get_booleans for the body: one Union and three ordered Difference modifiers should reference the separate editable base/cutters. Check source dimensions and transforms, get_bounds/get_geometry_diagnostics, then capture_scene_preview of the body in front and isometric views at the current revision.

One undo at the returned revision removes the whole applied batch. Undo affects the editor’s latest action, including manual actions, so check the revision and ask for the intended scope before undoing unrelated work.

Other workflows

For direct editing, send the same steps and revision to preview_changes, inspect the source-cache dry-run, then apply_changes. Proposal and direct-batch APIs are separate; do not nest a proposal in apply_changes. Standalone enclosure recipes use propose_enclosure and cannot be mixed with connector commands in the same batch. Discover strict live schemas for each tool rather than guessing fields.

title: Build an enclosure
description: An editable box and removable lid, with physical dimensions.
body:
Create the base and lid

Open Enclosure → New enclosure. Enter a name, inner width/depth/height, wall and floor thickness, corner radius and lid dimensions in mm. Inner height is floor-to-top-edge; the lid lip uses some space at the top. The outside W × D × H readout describes the base without its lid.

Use the lid clearance deliberately: it is the gap between the lip and inside wall on each side. A value such as 0.3 mm is a design choice to test, not a promise that your printer will produce a perfect fit. Choose Preview changes, review the result, then Create enclosure. Inspect its parts and save a native copy.

Update without starting again

Select an existing enclosure and choose Edit selected. Revise dimensions and Apply changes. Validation checks relationships such as wall, rim and lip sizes. If a change is refused, read the reason and adjust the dimensions instead of bypassing checks.

Cutouts and mounting

Associative feature tools support bounded wall cutouts, floor mounting patterns and named frames. On desktop, expand Enclosure → Cutouts & mounting for Wall cutout and Mounting posts. The modelling/MCP workflow also exposes these operations. Quest feature-panel capture and hardware verification are pending. Use live capability/schema discovery before sending a feature command.

Choose the correct wall/frame, then define size and position in physical units. Floor mounting patterns need deliberate spacing, support and screw clearance. Re-evaluate after changing the enclosure dimensions: a feature that was valid can become too close to an edge. Export base and lid as separate printable parts when needed.

Before making the real part

Measure the object that must fit inside, allow space for cables and fasteners, and print a small clearance coupon or a partial test first. The existing successful enclosure-and-lid print is one real-world example, not general acceptance for other models, materials or printers.

title: Make a printable enclosure
description: Create a box and separate lid, review clearance and export both components. Allow about 30 minutes.
body:
Before you begin

Use the desktop editor and a fresh Empty scene project. Hide the empty layer. Keep room for the recipe’s generated layers and have a slicer ready. The following values are a small teaching example; they do not describe a previously printed user project.

1. Set the inside and shell

  1. Scroll the left panel to Enclosure and choose New enclosure.
  2. Name it Practice enclosure. Set Inside size: Width 24, Depth 20, Height 14 mm.
  3. Under Walls & base, set Wall 3, Floor 3 and Corner radius 4 mm.
  4. Read Outside · W × D × H: the base should be 30 × 26 × 17 mm, without its lid.

2. Give the lid room

  1. Under Lid set Clearance 0.3, Lip depth 4 and Thickness 3 mm.
  2. Choose Preview changes. Inspect the proposed recipe and any validation feedback.
  3. Choose Create enclosure only when the preview is ready.
  4. Inspect the separate base and lid in Layers. Save and download a .form before adjusting either.

Clearance is the gap on each side between the lip and inside wall. The lip occupies some inside height. These values need a test on your printer and material.

3. Check the pair

  1. Open Assembly → Check fit.
  2. Pick the base and lid, using the scene or layer list. Read the chosen pair before continuing.
  3. Open Fit settings & accuracy and review Desired gap (mm), resolution and warnings.
  4. Inspect the lip and wall from multiple angles. A sampled report can miss thin intersections; it cannot guarantee a physical fit.
  5. To revise the recipe, select the enclosure, use Enclosure → Edit selected, change clearance, then Preview changes → Apply changes.

To inspect inside, select Enclosure Lid, open Primitives → Edit selected → Position, rotation & scale and set Position X to 45 mm, leaving Y and Z unchanged. This moves the lid aside in model space; save the assembled version first and use Undo to restore its pose before an assembled fit check.

4. Export the components

  1. Open Assembly → Parts & export. Review the base and lid printable-part boundaries and membership.
  2. If a boundary is missing, select the intended root and use Make selected layer a printable part. Do not assign the lid to the base part.
  3. Choose Export visible parts separately to produce separate STL components. Printable-part exports use calibrated physical size and do not apply experimental curved reduction.
  4. Open each STL in your slicer. Confirm base size, wall/floor continuity and the lid lip. Orient each component deliberately and review sliced layers.

Expected outcome: an editable enclosure recipe with a separate lid and separate STL components ready for slicer review. Print a small clearance coupon or a partial rim first.

Resolve common snags

  • Create enclosure is disabled: choose Preview changes and resolve validation feedback first.
  • A recipe is refused: check that the wall, corner radius, lip and clearance leave valid material.
  • Fit says unknown or sampled: inspect the stated limits; do not treat it as a pass.
  • Only one mesh exports: check part membership and visibility before exporting separately.
  • The lid is tight: test a revised clearance on a short rim before printing another full box.

Quest and next steps

Use desktop for this numeric recipe and file downloads. Quest can inspect the same project and use the supported assembly controls; Quest screenshots and hardware acceptance are pending. Continue with cutouts and mounting or export checks.

title: Assemble parts & check fit
description: Keep part boundaries clear and inspect the relationship.
body:
Check a pair

Open Assembly → Check fit, then choose two layers using the scene or list. Under Fit settings & accuracy set Desired gap (mm). The report is an approximate sampled check: it can miss thin features and collisions. Review the reported resolution and warnings. No result guarantees physical print-fit.

Alignment and connectors

Alignment offers Pick two layers, Centres, Bounding faces and Axes, with mate axis, offset and optional Match opposite normals. Bounds alignment can be helpful for a box, but does not prove that detailed surfaces mate.

Peg & socket lets you choose the peg layer, socket layer and joint face. Half the peg sits inside its layer. Set peg diameter, length and radial clearance. Advanced sizes & numeric placement provides socket diameter/depth, position and rotation, plus Use matching socket sizes. Inspect wall thickness around the socket after creating it.

Printable parts and preview

Under Parts & export, Make selected layer a printable part defines a root and its children. Assign selected to first part, Detach selected layer and Remove first part boundary control membership. Rename, move, hide and lock parts through Layers.

Show assembly preview is for inspecting the assembly arrangement. It does not replace source editing. Export first part STL or Export visible parts separately evaluates the part geometry and uses calibrated dimensions. These part exports do not apply experimental curved reduction. Keep a native project with the editable sources.

title: Projects, .form & recovery
description: Know which copy of your work lives where.
body:
The browser library

The logo menu → Library opens saved projects. Create a project, open a saved entry or inspect its details. A normal header Save click saves to this browser’s local library. The status icon distinguishes saved and unsaved state. Library data belongs to this browser profile and origin: another hostname, port or browser may show a different library.

A portable native copy

Hold the header Save icon to download .form, or use Download .form in library details. Open Project imports a native file through the desktop picker. This preserves editable project data instead of flattening everything into an export mesh. Save another copy before major restructuring, resampling or Bake. Older app versions may refuse newer projects, including projects above the old eight-layer limit.

An STL or GLB is a delivery mesh. A .form file is your working project. Keep both when you need to print today and revise later. Downloading does not create a shared cloud library.

Recovery is a safety net

The editor keeps local recovery checkpoints for interrupted work. A restored scene may show Recovery restored; inspect it before deciding which version to keep. Save the recovered result as a deliberate library/native copy. Existing checkpoints are retained when starting a new project, but recovery and browser storage are not an external backup.

If a library looks empty, check the exact origin and browser profile first. Do not clear site data as a troubleshooting first step. Private browsing, storage pressure or clearing browser data can remove local projects. Keep downloaded native copies in your own backup location.

Opening another project

Save your current changes before New Project or Open Project. These replace the open scene and start its own history; Undo is not a file-versioning system. File import, export and library downloads may require the desktop browser interface even when the modelling session uses VR.

Keep a shape you love

Made a curved handle, a favourite clay flourish or a useful part? Personal Shapes lets you keep its evaluated geometry independently of the project. Each insertion becomes an editable sculpt. The original primitive, Boolean and procedural construction history is flattened; keep your original .form project if you want to change that construction later.

  1. Select the sculpt you want to keep. For a live Boolean object, select its result/root, not a cutter. Unrelated layers are excluded. For a standalone analytic primitive, Bake it to a sculpt first at your chosen quality. Groups are not collections in this phase; select an individual child or Boolean root.
  2. In the left project controls, choose Personal Shapes… → Save selected as Shape. Wait for the evaluated thumbnail.
  3. Check the genuine preview and dimensions. Give it a name and choose Centre or Base centre as its insertion pivot, then choose Save Shape.
  4. Create or open another project. Open Personal Shapes… and choose Insert. Repeat to make another copy. Copies initially overlap at the insertion pivot; move them apart using the layer Move controls.
  5. Move, rotate, resize and sculpt either copy normally. Editing one copy does not edit the library master or other copies. Undo and redo work for insertion.
  6. Save the project as .form. Inserted SDF geometry travels with that project and exports through the normal STL/GLB controls.

Names, physical dimensions, creation dates and thumbnails appear in the browser. Rename requires Confirm rename; Delete requires a separate confirmation. Closing or cancelling preparation keeps the project and existing saves. From Quest, use World Settings → Project → Personal Shapes to leave XR and continue in the browser; enter Studio or Passthrough again when ready. This route has not yet been accepted on physical Quest hardware.

Full-detail masters and storage

A sculpt master preserves every stored SDF sample and its orientation. Boolean results use cropped evaluated bounds and must fit the supported evaluation grid at source detail. If they cannot, saving refuses with an explanation instead of quietly reducing detail. Keep a .form backup or split the object. Storage uses lossless gzip where supported; thumbnails are separate previews, never the master.

The library belongs to this browser profile and site address, separately from Project Library and recovery. It survives app restarts and project changes. Clearing site data, switching browser/profile or opening another origin does not carry your shapes over. Use Export Library Backup to transfer the whole shape library; also keep .form backups of valuable construction originals. On quota, corruption or memory errors, existing records are kept; free browser space or use a smaller project. Personal shapes as sculpting stamps (8.0.1), editable component collections (8.1) and agent integration (8.2) remain future work.

Back up and restore Personal Shapes

  1. Open Personal Shapes… → Export Library Backup. The app checks every SDF master and thumbnail without changing saved shapes. Review the shape count and size, then choose Download Library Backup. Keep the single .cshapes file somewhere safe.
  2. In another browser profile or on another device, open Personal Shapes… → Import Library Backup and choose the file. Wait for integrity, master and thumbnail checks.
  3. Review new copies, identifier conflicts and duplicates before Confirm Import Library Backup. Cancel Import, Browse or Close / Cancel leaves existing shapes intact.

Import merges in one atomic transaction. Conflicting identifiers become independent copies; previously imported identical entries are skipped. Current shapes are never replaced. A failure or interruption rolls back the entire import. A first import into the original source profile can create conflict copies; subsequent imports skip those copies.

Version 1 contains exact native or lossless gzip SDF masters, names, timestamps, dimensions, calibration, pivots, original rendered thumbnails and SHA-256 integrity hashes. Hashes detect corruption, not publisher identity. Unsupported versions, damaged payloads and invalid thumbnails are refused before confirmation.

Safety limits: 100 shapes, 64 MiB total backup, 4 MiB manifest, and 32 MiB uncompressed per master, with a combined backup plus validation allowance of 224 MiB for validation memory. Open a project using at most 32 MiB tracked geometry before importing. Larger libraries/masters are refused without reducing detail; keep their .form originals. The library retains its 512 MiB storage budget. Browser storage estimates are checked when available; actual quota failures roll back atomically. A browser download request does not prove the file was saved—check your Downloads.

Quest uses the existing exit-XR browser route. File picking, downloads, quota estimates and large-library memory behaviour still need physical Quest acceptance. Custom stamps are unchanged.

title: Work from images & STL references
description: Bring a visual guide without turning it into sculpted material.
body:
Import on desktop

Use Import image or STL reference…. The current reference collection supports up to six records, with format, byte and decoded-resource validation. Import through the desktop file picker; exit XR to import and re-enter afterwards. A failed import leaves the existing references unchanged.

Place a reference

Select its entry to adjust visibility and locking. Use transform controls or Precise placement for position, rotation and scale. Image settings include anchor and further display controls. References can guide proportions and surface snapping but do not become Boolean solids or get included in sculpt mesh exports.

STL display sizing

Reference STL import normalises its display size. That presentation size is not evidence of its original physical units. Check and set the reference transform and calibration before using it as a physical guide. Measure known features rather than assuming an imported file is already 1:1.

Use images you own or have permission to use. Application captures in this guide come from a disposable browser session. Save your project after arranging references so you can return to the same setup.

title: Paint colour & protect with masks
description: Colour and protection have separate jobs.
body:
Paint without reshaping

Desktop Paint Colour adds surface colour; Erase Colour removes it. VR Paint is a button below the Tool Wheel; Options contains colour, paint operation and reset to layer base colour. Radius and strength help blend coverage. Paint works on sculpt geometry; Bake a primitive before painting.

Layer display colours and Normal/Matte/Glossy are viewport aids, separate from actual paint. Export GLB for a coloured mesh. STL carries geometry only, so a painted STL looks uncoloured in a slicer.

Mask areas you want to protect

Mask Paint adds protection; Mask Erase removes it. In VR choose Mask below the wheel and use Options for operation and overlay. Paint the protected region, switch to a sculpt brush and work nearby. Erase the mask when you want that area editable again.

If a brush seems weak or does nothing, inspect the mask, layer lock and active layer before increasing strength. Masks do not replace a separate layer for an independent movable part. Save a native copy to retain editable painting/masking state; an export mesh is not the full authoring project.

title: Export at the size you intend
description: Prepare, review, then download.
body:
Choose units and size first

Open Export…. File type and Quality preset share the first row. Actual size (1:1) is on by default and uses calibrated project dimensions. Turn it off to reveal target longest-side sizing; the casual default is 200 mm. Deliberate values such as 100 mm are supported. The summary shows Actual XYZ → Export XYZ, scale and quality before download.

STL uses millimetres and has no colour. GLB uses metres and can carry colour and layer transforms. A 100 mm part is 0.1 m in GLB. Changing a target size overrides project physical sizing for that export; it does not recalibrate the native project.

Choose the correct scope

Prepare exportMeaning
Current layerThe selected committed source surface. Scenes with live Boolean modifiers or enabled arrays refuse this shortcut and ask for the visible Boolean result.
All visible layersExcludes hidden unreferenced roots and references. STL evaluates visible layer subtraction/intersection; live modifiers/arrays also require evaluation. Plain separate source exports retain their source representation where evaluation is not required.
Unified BooleanOne evaluated composed SDF result, including ordered cutters and arrays, rather than raw cutter solids.
Printable part STLAssembly/part workflow evaluates the chosen part and children with calibrated dimensions. Visible parts can be exported separately.

GLB’s plain visible-layer path can preserve separate source layers and transforms; do not assume it performs STL’s visible ordered-layer composition. Choose Unified Boolean when you need the evaluated composed result. Hidden referenced operands still contribute to their target. Read the summary’s committed surface / evaluated SDF label.

Quality, detail and limits

Fast keeps prepared triangles. Standard welds and cleans. High additionally simplifies supported flat regions while retaining holes and sharp edges. High is not a promise to reduce curved triangles. Triangle estimate is metadata-only and uncertain; preparation reports actual generated counts.

Advanced settings offers Default · up to 192³ and Extra detail · up to 256³ for evaluated Boolean/part export. These are maximum sampling grids, not guaranteed final resolutions or triangle counts. More detail uses more memory and work; it cannot rescue an invalid model. Export memory starts at 256 MiB with larger configured choices. Source-sampling work, intermediate mesh, triangle and memory ceilings can refuse an export even if preview works. Do not bypass refusals; reduce complexity, split parts or choose a lower cap.

Review and download

  1. Choose scope and wait through preparation, evaluation, meshing, optimisation, sizing, validation and encoding as applicable.
  2. Inspect the generated triangle count, dimensions, topology warnings and Print report. Estimated memory is admission accounting, not a measured whole-browser peak.
  3. Use the prepared file link to download. Changing relevant settings invalidates a prepared result.
  4. In your slicer verify mm interpretation, orientation, scale, closed surfaces, wall thickness, cavities and clearances. Look at layer previews for missing thin features.

Cancel or Escape stops active export. Switching windows or hiding the tab should continue it. Real lifecycle interruptions and failures report their stage/cause; an interrupted export is not a completed file. Source sampling can miss sub-grid features, so no topology or sampled fit check replaces inspecting the actual exported mesh and a physical test.

Should I use curved reduction?

Leave Curved reduction · Experimental · STL off for the normal exporter. The optional Surface tolerance choices are 0.01, 0.025, 0.05 and 0.1 mm. This stage runs after physical STL sizing and keeps original vertex positions; it is unavailable for GLB and is not applied to printable-part exports.

The candidate must pass checks for a closed surface, matching dimensions and topology structure, sampled distances in both directions between the original and reduced surface, outlines and sections through cavities or gaps. Borders, sharp creases and outermost points are protected. Separate processing-work and temporary-memory limits still apply. A rejected candidate returns the original bytes and reports ✕ fallback with a reason; an accepted candidate reports ✓ applied. Sampled checks are not a fit guarantee. Compare a slicer section and test the physical clearance before relying on a fitted part.

title: Connect a local modelling agent
description: MCP lets an agent inspect and propose work in your active editor.
body:
Start the optional bridge

Use Node 22+ and install repository dependencies. Normal npm run dev does not expose agent access. For the bridge:

npm run dev:agent
# If the default port is occupied:
npm run dev:agent -- --port 5197

Open the exact matching editor origin printed in the terminal. Vite listens on 0.0.0.0 and the bridge uses an assigned port. Localhost/127.0.0.1 works on the host; the machine .local hostname or private LAN IP supports local-network devices. Use matching hostname/IP for the browser origin. The agent HTTP workflow is separate from WebXR’s secure-origin requirement.

Configure Codex

Replace the absolute repository path below with your checkout path. This is a local stdio adapter launched by the client, not a remote HTTP MCP URL.

codex mcp add centra_sculpt -- node /ABS/REPO/scripts/agent-mcp.mjs

Or add to your user ~/.codex/config.toml:

[mcp_servers.centra_sculpt]
command = "node"
args = ["/ABS/REPO/scripts/agent-mcp.mjs"]
tool_timeout_sec = 20

Use an absolute Node executable if the desktop client cannot find Node. Refresh/restart its MCP connection and inspect the available tools. Configuration reference: official OpenAI MCP guide, checked 10 November 2026.

Configure Cursor

Use project .cursor/mcp.json or user ~/.cursor/mcp.json, then enable/restart the server in MCP settings:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "centra_sculpt": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/ABS/REPO/scripts/agent-mcp.mjs"]
    }
  }
}

See Cursor’s MCP configuration. No client configuration is changed automatically by Centra Sculpt.

Approve the connection, then editing

In Local agent access (development), choose Approve connection. Default access is read-only. Allow editing (includes Undo) separately permits mutations and proposal staging. Revoke access disconnects it. One browser tab owns the bridge; revoke there before handing over to another tab. Multiple MCP clients share the approved session, without per-client grants.

The bridge discovers ignored work/agent-session.json; credentials rotate on restart. Never publish that file or its token. This is local developer access, not an internet/multi-user security boundary. The development editor and bridge are reachable on your LAN. Approve a session you control, and stop the server when finished. There are no agent save/load/export, arbitrary-code or filesystem tools; normal editor recovery still records approved modelling changes.

Discover before writing

  1. Call scene_summary {} and retain its exact revision.
  2. Call get_capabilities {}; compare version, buildVersion, sessionId and tool inventory with the client’s MCP panel / tools/list.
  3. Read only what you need: list_objects, get_object, get_booleans, get_array, get_bounds and get_geometry_diagnostics.
  4. Use a reviewed proposal or preview_changes → apply_changes for one atomic command batch. Both dry-run and proposal staging need editing permission.
  5. After applying, inspect returned IDs, graph and bounds, then request scoped front/isometric captures.

Use exactly one objectId or partId for isolated capture_scene_preview scope. Captures report evaluated visible bounds; source bounds may be conservative. Neither is a topology or print-fit certificate.

title: Agent troubleshooting
description: Recover the connection without repeating uncertain writes.
body:
SymptomNext step
agent_access / disconnectedCheck dev:agent is running, open its matching origin, reconnect MCP and approve the current browser session.
Read-only / permission_deniedConnection approval and Allow editing are separate. Proposal staging and dry-run also require editing. Browser proposal approval is another deliberate step.
revision_conflictGet a fresh scene_summary, inspect changes and rebuild the complete plan against that revision.
busyFinish/cancel the active editor operation. Do not queue another mutation.
Missing tools or stale schemaCompare get_capabilities build/session and tools/list with the client panel. Refresh/restart MCP after code/schema updates.
Restarted development serverThe scene can remain open while the tab detects restart; approve the new session explicitly. Credentials have rotated.
Timeout during a writeDo not automatically retry. Inspect scene_summary, list_objects, proposal state and history to determine whether it committed.
Rejected proposalDo not apply or resubmit automatically. Read get_proposal and revise only with the person’s direction.
Resource/layer refusalRespect the 16-layer and sampling/mesh/memory limits. Simplify the plan or split work.

Coordinate mistakes

Mutation tools require expectedRevision. Length unit is mm, cm or in; scale is dimensionless. Full object.transform rotations use XYZ radians, while rotate_object uses rotationDegrees. move_object defaults to a world-axis offset; mode set replaces position. rotate_object by rotates around the object origin, not around the world origin. Client JSON must match the strict schema; unknown fields are rejected.

Capture and fit mistakes

A source-cache dry-run does not validate evaluated Boolean topology. A pretty preview is not a print report. Inspect the graph and evaluated scope, then perform the normal export and slicer checks. Client-specific cached tool exposure and real Quest acceptance cannot be proven by repository tests alone.

title: FAQ & current limitations
description: Practical answers when the result surprises you.
body:
Why can I see a cutter in Layers?

Layers displays editable ingredients. Switch to Boolean to inspect the composed result and choose an evaluated export scope. A hidden referenced cutter can still affect its target.

Why does the exported size differ?

Check calibration, Actual size (1:1), target longest side and STL mm versus GLB m. Reference STL display normalisation is not original physical scale. Review the export XYZ summary before downloading.

Why does a brush do nothing?

Check the selected layer, lock, mask and tool mode. Primitive sources need Bake to Sculpt Layer for brushing/painting. Finish an active Move or other busy operation before starting another.

Why can preview work but export fail?

Preview can use reduced detail. Export evaluates under its own strict source-work, mesh, triangle and memory limits. Arrays and hidden referenced operands still cost work. Lower detail or simplify/split parts; a higher memory selection does not remove every limit.

Will High or 256³ make a perfect print?

No. Sampling can miss thin walls, tiny holes, cone tips and narrow gaps. High simplifies eligible flat regions, not arbitrary curved surfaces. Experimental curved reduction is optional and sampled, with original fallback. Check the exported mesh in your slicer and test physical clearances.

Where is the Personal Shape Library?

Choose Personal Shapes… in the left project controls to save an evaluated sculpt and insert independent editable copies. See the save-and-reuse guide. Personal shapes as stamps are deferred to 8.0.1; editable component collections and agent integration follow in 8.1 and 8.2.

Is everything tested on Quest and printers?

No. Automated tests and desktop browser checks are useful evidence, but Phase 7.6 does not claim Quest hardware acceptance. One successful enclosure/lid print does not validate every model or printer. Fit checks and sampled geometry diagnostics have explicit limits.

Can I read this offline?

The built site and Pagefind bundle have no runtime account/API dependency. Serve the output with a static HTTP server; opening files directly can block browser module/search loading. Cache availability depends on your browser; this site does not install an offline service worker.

Recover a Boolean preview

  1. Release active tools and wait for the preview to finish.
  2. Check the target, operand IDs, modifier order and enabled state.
  3. Switch Surface View to Boolean. Hidden referenced operands still contribute.
  4. If the status says Reduced detail, inspect small features in the prepared export. Preview may lower resolution to stay within its unchanged budget.
  5. For a refusal, simplify arrays or sources, or split the job. Export does not automatically inherit the preview downgrade.

Recover an STL or GLB export

Check the selected scope first. STL evaluated scopes include live operations; GLB separate-layer output has different composition semantics. Current layer refuses live modifiers/arrays. Recheck calibration, scale, Actual size (1:1) and the XYZ summary. STL values are mm; GLB values are metres. Wait for the prepared download link, then inspect the file in a slicer or viewer. Save a .form before restructuring a design to fit resource limits.

How do I move or protect my Personal Shapes?

Use Personal Shapes… → Export Library Backup, then Download Library Backup. On the destination, choose Import Library Backup, review the validated preview and confirm. The .cshapes file preserves full SDF masters, dimensions, pivots and genuine thumbnails. Existing shapes remain; identifier conflicts create copies and repeat imports skip previously imported identical entries. Errors and interrupted imports roll back. Clearing site data still removes local shapes, so keep the downloaded file elsewhere. See backup limits and restore instructions. Quest file transfer still needs hardware acceptance.

title: Choose how to build
description: Start with the kind of change you need, then choose a tool.
body:
Choose a starting point

Your taskChooseKeep in mind
A measured body, hole cutter or ringPrimitivesDimensions stay editable until you Bake.
Add or remove organic massClayBrush strokes use sampled clay; start broad and refine.
Pull a region or twist a ridgeMove ToolDeforms a surface region. Transform Layer moves the whole object.
Join solids or make openingsBooleansKeep operands editable and check operation order.
Brush or paint a generated resultBakeCreates sampled clay. Keep original sources and inspect thin features.

A useful sequence

For a holder, start with primitives, position them in mm and use Booleans for slots. Save the editable design. Bake only if you need a sculpted finish; it is not required just to export an evaluated STL.

Desktop and Quest

Desktop suits numeric entry and file handling. Quest suits spatial inspection and hand-guided sculpting. Workspace navigation changes your view, while a layer transform changes the object. See desktop controls and Quest roles and gestures.

What is available?

Brushes, built-in Stamp shapes, primitives, live Booleans, arrays, enclosure recipes, assemblies and the project library are implemented. Curved STL reduction is optional and experimental. Use Personal Shapes to save and insert reusable sculpt geometry. The desktop panel labelled SHAPE LIBRARY holds built-in stamps. Personal stamps are deferred to 8.0.1.

title: Modelling words, explained
description: A plain-language companion to the controls and print reports.
body:
Shapes and surfaces

Primitive
A shape defined by editable parameters, such as box width or cylinder diameter.
Voxel / SDF
A voxel is a sample in a 3D grid. A signed distance field describes distance from a surface, with a sign distinguishing inside from outside.
Mesh / triangle
A surface made of connected triangles. An exported mesh is different from editable project sources.
Tangent plane
A small flat plane touching a surface at one point. Flatten uses this local reference rather than a measured cutting plane.
Resolution
The sampling detail, such as 64³. Increasing it costs memory and cannot recover detail already lost.
Bake
Evaluate a result into sampled sculpt geometry. Keep the original ingredients so you can revise them.

Combining and placing

Boolean
A solid operation: union joins, difference removes, intersect keeps shared volume.
Operand / cutter
A source shape used by an operation. A cutter is an operand used for subtraction.
Array
Repeated evaluated instances of one source, arranged linearly or radially.
Transform
Position, rotation and scale. Local axes follow the object; world axes follow the project.
Calibration
The relationship between model units and real physical units.
Printable part
A defined root and its children evaluated together for a component export.

Checking a print

Clearance
Intentional space between mating surfaces. Printer and material variation still need testing.
Watertight / closed topology
A mesh with closed boundaries. It is useful for printing but does not prove strength, correct size or fit.
Sampled check
A check at finite points or sections; small problems between samples may be missed.
Fallback
The original export is retained when optional reduction cannot pass its safeguards.
STL / GLB
STL carries triangles and is interpreted in millimetres in this workflow. GLB uses metres and supports colour. Neither replaces a .form backup.

Continue with choosing tools or troubleshooting.
